title: Audio Asset Lifecycle, Interchange, Rights, Review & Publication

selection_basis.reduced_strict_order: MSAS-01 → MSAS-03 → MSAS-04 → MSAS-05 → MSAS-07 → MSAS-09 → MSAS-12 → MSAS-14 → MSAS-15 → MSAS-18 → MSAS-21
selection_basis.parallel_lanes: MRCS-12 remains selected_not_started; MVPS-18 remains selected_not_started.

objective: Implement the audio-asset lifecycle seam spanning version/variant/localization review, structured interchange and round-trip loss reporting, middleware bridge identity preservation, rights/consent/provenance/sample/voice identity evidence and governed publication intent, while delegating generic resource/review/rights infrastructure to ARI/PCA and keeping generated content candidate-only until explicit acceptance and registration.
boundaries: MSAS-01 through MSAS-15 remain prior studio, semantic, voice, spatial and live-control foundations consumed by this tranche.
ARI plus PCA-01/PCA-15 retain generic resource identity, derivative lineage, rights/use capability, provenance, review/locking/dependency and asset-governance authority.
PCA-09 retains provider-neutral generation orchestration; generated music/SFX/voice output remains candidate content until explicit acceptance and ARI registration.
PCA-13 retains generic localization-production infrastructure; MSAS-18 reviews and binds audio variants without replacing localization authority.
Structured interchange and middleware round-trip preserve canonical AAI semantic IDs where supported and report unsupported/lossy semantics explicitly rather than silently normalizing them.
Rights, consent, sample-source and voice-identity evidence are referenced from owning authorities and may block publication when missing; MSAS does not infer permission.
Review acceptance/rejection/supersession preserves prior versions and provenance rather than deleting history.
Publication intent is governed creator state and cannot itself perform external provider publication, spend money, bypass rights gates or mutate gameplay/world truth.
Provider-off/local-first lifecycle and interchange remain blocking-capable.
Meaningful spoken/sonic content retains transcript/caption or semantic non-audio alternatives where applicable.
MSAS-21 remains unauthorized until separately selected.
MRCS and MVPS lane state remains independent.
next_action: On an MSAS-specific owner Continue, fresh-read the MSAS-18 dependency closure and msas lane-state ref, then start and execute the bounded tranche under OPS3 v3.10 / OPS3-11.
